context.title: Josiah Seeks God Young
context.summary: Josiah begins seeking God as a teenager and purges idols from Judah and the north. During temple repairs the book of the law is found; Josiah humbles himself and leads the people in covenant renewal.
context.background: Chronicles places Josiah's purge in his twelfth year, before the book was found in his eighteenth (vv. 3, 8), while Kings tells the reforms after the discovery. Burning the false priests' bones on their altars (v. 5) fulfilled the prophecy of 1 Kings 13:2.

customs.note: Better 'the second quarter' — a newer district of Jerusalem where the prophetess Huldah lived.

watchFor: 'While he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David' (v. 3).

people.name: Josiah
people.summary: Healed by Jehovah, or Jehovah will support. The son of Amon, and his successor on the throne of Judah (2 Kings 22:1; 2 Chr. 34:1). His history is contained in 2 Kings 22, 23.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26).

people.name: Shaphan
people.summary: A coney, a scribe or secretary of king Josiah (2 Kings 22:3-7). He consulted Huldah concerning the newly-discovered copy of the law which was delivered to him by Hilkiah the priest (8-14).

people.name: Joah
people.summary: Son of Joahaz, and “recorder” or keeper of the state archives under King Josiah (2 Chr. 34:8).

people.name: Joahaz
people.summary: (2 Chr. 34:8), a contracted form of Jehoahaz.

people.name: Maaseiah
people.summary: One who was sent by king Josiah to repair the temple (2 Chr. 34:8).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: The high priest in the reign of Josiah (1 Chr. 6:13; Ezra 7:1). To him and his deputy (2 Kings 23:5), along with the ordinary priests and the Levites who had charge of the gates, was entrusted the purification of the temple in Jerusalem.

people.name: Merari
people.summary: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).

people.name: Jahath
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the overseers of the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A Levite who superintended the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: The Lord has remembered.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Ahikam
people.summary: Brother of support = helper, one of the five whom Josiah sent to consult the prophetess Huldah in connection with the discovery of the book of the law (2 Kings 22:12-14; 2 Chr. 34:20).

people.name: Achbor
people.summary: The son of Micah, one of those whom Josiah sent to the prophetess Huldah to ascertain from her the meaning of the recently discovered book of the law (2 Chr. 34:20).

people.name: Asahiah
people.summary: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

people.name: Michaiah
people.summary: 2 Kings 22:12.

people.name: Hasrah
people.summary: Poverty, “keeper of the wardrobe,” i.e., of the sacerdotal vestments (2 Chr. 34:22); called Harhas 2 Kings 22:14.

people.name: Huldah
people.summary: Weasel, a prophetess; the wife of Shallum. She was consulted regarding the “book of the law” discovered by the high priest Hilkiah (2 Kings 22:14-20; 2 Chr. 34:22-28).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: Keeper of the temple vestments in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:14).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Second Quarter
places.summary: Heb. mishneh (2 Kings 22:14; 2 Chr. 34:22), rendered in Revised Version “second quarter”, the residence of the prophetess Huldah. The Authorized Version followed the Jewish commentators, who, following the Targum, gave the Hebrew word its post-Biblical sense, as if it meant a place of instruction.
